rules: Every shortcut is local to the Vitre window and works only while Vitre has focus. Never use Electron globalShortcut or RegisterHotKey, and never install a low-level keyboard hook.

Browser-first keys never reach the page. They are Chrome's reserved set: Ctrl+T, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+F4, Ctrl+Shift+W, Ctrl+Shift+T, Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+Shift+Tab, Ctrl+Page Up and Ctrl+Page Down. Vitre adds three: F6 and Shift+F6; Esc Esc and Ctrl+W while a peek is open; and Esc or F11 to leave full screen or pointer lock. Shift+right-click is the mouse equivalent. Electron doesn't inherit Chrome's reserved list, so catch these keys in before-input-event on every WebContents (tab, peek, PDF guest, chrome view, menu layer) and call preventDefault.

Page-first keys go to the page first, and Vitre acts only if the page didn't call preventDefault. This covers every other key Vitre binds outside its own surfaces: Ctrl+F, F3, Shift+F3, Ctrl+G, Ctrl+Shift+G, Ctrl+L, Alt+D, Ctrl+H, Ctrl+J, Ctrl+Shift+D, Ctrl+Shift+A, Ctrl+Q, Alt+Enter in a peek, Alt+Left, Alt+Right, Ctrl+R, F5, the hard-reload keys, Ctrl+P, Ctrl+S, Ctrl+U, Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9, Ctrl+Shift+Page Up/Down, the zoom keys, Ctrl+comma, F1, Ctrl+Shift+Delete, F11 to enter, F12, Ctrl+Shift+I/J/C, a single Esc, Shift+F10, the Menu key, and Shift+click and the other link clicks. They run on Chromium's unhandled-key path through hidden application-menu accelerators. The fallback is a preload that reads event.defaultPrevented after dispatch.

Local keys work only while focus is in a Vitre surface: the address field, find field, switcher, menus, panels, peek header, tab bar or Home. They never reach a page. While a menu or the latched switcher is open, global keys are swallowed.

Pages can never block these: F6, which always takes focus out of the page; the reserved tab and window keys (Ctrl+T, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+F4, Ctrl+Shift+W, Ctrl+Shift+T, Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+Shift+Tab, Ctrl+Page Up/Down); Esc Esc and Ctrl+W on a peek; leaving full screen or pointer lock; and Shift+right-click. From the address pill (F6), every page-first key goes straight to Vitre, so F6 then the key is the general route; menus add Reload, Find on page…, Print…, Inspect, Show downloads, Full screen and Settings.

Only keyboard lock (navigator.keyboard.lock in element full screen) sends the browser-first keys to the page first. Plain element full screen and pointer lock keep them browser-first. Esc (held, under keyboard lock) and F11 always leave. F11 window full screen is not element full screen.

AltGr guard: a binding that uses Alt needs Ctrl up and AltGraph off, and a binding that uses Ctrl needs Alt up. Modifiers must match exactly: Ctrl+Alt+Left is not Alt+Left, and Ctrl+Alt+Tab is not Ctrl+Tab. Either the left or right Ctrl and Alt work, but nothing depends on the right-hand key.
IME guard: no shortcut fires while isComposing is true or keyCode is 229. Esc closes the IME first.

Layouts: match letters by virtual key, which follows the key's label, so QWERTZ, AZERTY and Dvorak behave like every Windows app and Cyrillic or Greek layouts still give Ctrl+C. Match digits by virtual key or physical code. Match Plus, Minus and Equals by the character the active layout types, with VK_OEM_PLUS/MINUS and the numpad as fallbacks; zoom wins when a digit key types - or +. Only letters, digits, F keys, navigation keys, Enter, Esc, Tab, Backspace, Delete, Plus, Minus, Equals and comma carry shortcuts. Comma is matched by VK_OEM_COMMA.

Held-Ctrl states: no chord that holds Ctrl may rely on Esc, because Ctrl+Esc opens Start. The switcher latches, staying open with Ctrl up, on the first typed character, on Ctrl+Shift+A, when opened by mouse, and when Sticky Keys is on. Losing window focus (Start, Alt+Tab, the Win key) cancels back to the starting tab.

Key repeat is ignored for anything that closes, opens, reopens or toggles: Ctrl+W, Ctrl+F4, Ctrl+Shift+W, Ctrl+Shift+T, Ctrl+N, F11, F12, F1, Ctrl+J, Ctrl+comma, Ctrl+Shift+A, Ctrl+Shift+D, Alt+Enter, Ctrl+Q, every Esc step, and Alt+Left or Browser Back when it closes a peek.

Esc unwinds one layer per fresh keydown (key repeat never steps the ladder), in this order: the IME; a Vitre menu; a Vitre popover, prompt or page dialog; the latched switcher; element full screen or pointer lock; the Settings or Downloads panel; the focused Vitre field (the address field first puts the address back, then returns to the page; the find field closes find); the page; parked find; the peek; and finally stop loading. An Esc used by any layer never counts toward a peek’s Esc Esc.

Topmost surface: Ctrl+W, Esc, Ctrl+F and the page keys (reload, print, save, source, zoom, developer tools) act on an open panel first, then a peek, then the tab — the same order as the Esc ladder and as they are drawn. Tab and window keys always act on the window, and leaving a tab warm-closes its peek.

Peek's Shift+click and Shift+Enter come only from setWindowOpenHandler, and only when all of these hold: the disposition is 'new-window'; details.features is empty, so sign-in, payment and call pop-ups stay real pop-ups; within about 500 ms the preload saw a trusted Shift+click or Shift+Enter on a link whose href equals the URL; the URL is http, https or file and isn't only a #fragment change; and the Shift+click setting is on. Otherwise Vitre behaves exactly like Chrome, and it never adds a Shift+click listener of its own.

Windows conventions keep working. Alt+F4 closes the window, and Alt+Space opens the system menu on the frameless window. Alt or F10 pressed alone only closes an open Vitre menu: there is no native menu bar, no & mnemonics, autoHideMenuBar stays off, and handled Alt chords don't beep. Shift+F10 and the Menu key open the context menu. CUA keys, Ctrl+Backspace and Ctrl+Left/Right Shift text direction work in every Vitre field.

No single printable key is ever a shortcut on the page or in the bar, so screen-reader browse mode and site keys (YouTube, Gmail) keep them. Single keys work only inside Vitre's own focused widgets: menu access keys and switcher search.

Every F-key action has a non-F route for laptops without Fn lock: F3 → Ctrl+G, F5 → Ctrl+R, F6 → Ctrl+L, F11 → Full screen in the + menu, F12 → Ctrl+Shift+I, F1 → Ctrl+comma, Shift+F10 → the Menu key or a right-click.

Display: keys appear only as plain dim text in menus, tooltips and Settings › Keyboard shortcuts, never as chips, badges or key tips. Windows spelling, no spaces (Ctrl+Shift+T, Shift+click, Page Up, Delete). Letters and digits print by their Latin key names; comma, Plus, Minus and Equals print the active layout’s label. Modifier names are localized with the UI.

Held switcher: while the switcher is open, held or latched, every Ctrl+letter except Ctrl+W is a search character and never its global command (so Ctrl+T, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+Shift+T and Ctrl+Shift+W do nothing there). The first key is translated with the active layout as if Ctrl were up; with an IME on, it only latches and the IME takes the next key.

Address field: Shift+Delete removes a history suggestion only when the user moved onto that row with Up/Down or the pointer is on it; the default top match never counts, and otherwise Shift+Delete cuts.

Hardware keys: Browser Back/Forward/Refresh/Stop/Search/Home and the mouse side buttons arrive through app-command and act like Alt+Left, Alt+Right, Ctrl+R, Esc (stop), Ctrl+L and the Home tab, on the peek first where that applies.
changes: TabMotion 'Esc while switching': in the held deck, cancel is now 'Ctrl+Shift+Tab back to the card you started on, then release Ctrl', a click on the wallpaper, or switching away from Vitre (any loss of focus cancels). Esc cancels only once the switcher is latched. Why: with Ctrl held, Esc is Ctrl+Esc, which Windows takes to open Start.

Typing while switching (SettingsTabs, TabSearch): the first character typed latches the switcher open, so Ctrl can be let go and the field accepts IME input, AltGr characters and dead keys. Enter opens the tab and Esc cancels; while Ctrl is held, W still closes the card. Write this on TabSearch, which has no key notes yet. Why: IMEs can't compose with Ctrl down, AltGr letters arrive as Ctrl+Alt, and a Shift tapped under Ctrl switches the keyboard layout.

The switcher's latched mode is now specified for Deck, Grid and Strip. It is latched when opened with Ctrl+Shift+A, by typing, by mouse, or with Sticky Keys on. Latched keys: Left/Right, arrow keys in Grid, Enter, Esc. In Grid and Strip, Tab with Ctrl held moves in reading order. Ctrl+Tab is ignored while Alt or AltGr is down. With 'Order of tabs: Tab bar order', Ctrl+Tab and its quick tap go to the tab on the right. Why: releasing Ctrl can't confirm a choice when Ctrl isn't held, Sticky Keys lets go of Ctrl after one key, and AltGr+Tab is Windows' persistent task switcher.
Ctrl+W in the switcher while a search is filtering closes only the highlighted result. Why: the case in mock issue #29 was unspecified.

Ctrl+Shift+T now has one meaning: reopen from a single recently-closed list of tabs, peeks and windows, newest first. A peek reopens as a peek if its source tab is active, otherwise as a tab. The + menu row's label names what it will reopen ('Reopen closed tab', '…peek', '…window'), as Chrome's does. Why: the + menu and PeekSpec gave the same global key two different meanings.

Priorities are now stated for designed and printed keys that had none. Page-first: Alt+Enter on a peek, Ctrl+Q, Ctrl+Shift+A, Ctrl+L, Ctrl+J, Shift+F10 and the Menu key, and the printed page keys. Browser-first: Ctrl+W, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+Shift+T, Ctrl+Tab and F6. Why: Sheets, Excel, Jupyter and VS Code use Alt+Enter; Outlook uses Ctrl+Q; Slack and Teams use Ctrl+Shift+A; web terminals use Ctrl+L. Each of these keeps a route a page can't block (the header button, a header double-click, menus, Ctrl+Tab then typing, F6).

Ctrl+Q: it acts only on real http/https links and never while typing in a field. It now also peeks the highlighted suggestion in the address field, so Ctrl+Q is the peek key on every face of the pill. Why: one peek key everywhere, and javascript: links and buttons must never open a peek.

Esc Esc on a peek ignores key repeat and doesn't count an Esc already used by the IME, a menu, find or leaving full screen. Once you've typed in the peek, it only bumps the sheet, as a click on the dim already does; Ctrl+W and × still always close. Why: Vim, Jupyter, Figma and spreadsheet users press Esc twice on purpose. DESIGN-NOTES said Esc Esc 'always closes'.
Closing a peek, by any route, returns keyboard focus to the link that opened it. Why: PeekSpec didn't say where focus goes (mock issue #24).

Page keys with a peek open: Ctrl+S, Ctrl+U, zoom and F12 now act on the peek, as Ctrl+R, Ctrl+P and Ctrl+F already did. Tab and window keys act on the window, and leaving the tab warm-closes its peek. Why: the topmost-surface rule had been applied only in part.

Address field: Alt+Enter opens the address or result in a new foreground tab, and Ctrl+Enter adds www. and .com, as in Chrome and Edge. Mock issue #38's background-tab idea is not adopted. Why: 'Alt+Enter means as a tab, and go there' then holds for both the pill and the peek, and Peek already covers looking without leaving.

F6 becomes browser-first and gets a defined cycle: page ↔ address pill (or the find field while find is open). With a peek open it cycles peek page → peek header → address pill. Shift+F6 goes the other way, and Tab from the address field walks the tab bar. Why: a page could trap focus, FindSpec specified only half of F6, and no key reached the tab circles.

FindSpec's edge-case copy and DESIGN-NOTES Find › Keys: the guaranteed way to Vitre's find is 'F6, then Ctrl+F' (or Find on page… in the page menu), not 'Ctrl+L or F6'. Why: Ctrl+L is page-first, and web terminals and Word for the web take it.
Esc: the four partial orders (in Find, Peek, Menus and the switcher) are replaced by one ladder. Why: panels, address editing, element full screen and stop loading weren't covered by any of them.
Settings and Downloads panels: Esc and Ctrl+W close the panel, not the tab, and Ctrl+J and Ctrl+comma toggle their own panel. Why: only Ctrl+F was defined for panels.

The + circle menu gains a separator and 'Show downloads  Ctrl+J [S]', 'Full screen  F11 [F]' (a check item) and 'Settings  Ctrl+, [E]'. The + circle's tooltip reads 'New tab  Ctrl+T'. Why: Ctrl+J and Ctrl+comma are page-first and need a route a page can't block (the ring exists only during downloads, and Settings was reachable only from Home), and F11 needs a non-F route.
The Home wallpaper menu prints 'Settings  Ctrl+,'. 'Show tab bar' stays without a key. Why: the proposed Ctrl+Shift+B is Microsoft Pinyin's expressions panel.

Key spelling: 'Ctrl + Tab' and 'Ctrl + Shift + A' (SettingsTabs), 'Shift + click' (VideoStates), the spaced keys on the PeekSpec and TabMotion cards, 'Shift+Click' (CtxMenu link lists), 'Shift+Del' (CtxMenu suggestion row) and 'Shift-click to peek' (PeekDiscover) become 'Ctrl+Tab', 'Ctrl+Shift+A', 'Shift+click', 'Alt+Enter', 'Shift+Delete' and 'Shift+click to peek'. Why: two spellings on screen read as two systems, and Windows spelling is what the menus and FindSpec already use.

Guards widened: the AltGr guard, which covered only Alt+C, now covers every Alt and Ctrl chord. The composition guard, which covered only find's live search, now covers every shortcut. Why: Polish, Hungarian, Czech and German users type characters with AltGr, and the Japanese IME uses F6–F10 and Ctrl+U/I/O/P/T while composing.
Shift+Delete removes a history suggestion only while a suggestion row is highlighted; otherwise it stays the Windows cut. Why: CUA Shift+Delete means Cut in every Windows text field.
Ctrl+W, Ctrl+F4, Ctrl+Shift+W and Ctrl+Shift+T ignore key repeat, so holding Ctrl+W closes one tab, not a run of them. Why: an accidental hold shouldn't empty the window.

Shift+click gets a switch, 'Shift+click a link: Peek / Open in new window', on Settings › Keyboard shortcuts. This settles the open idea of a Peek group in Settings › Tabs. Why: Vitre changes Chrome's Shift+click, so Chrome's behaviour should be one switch away.

customization: Settings › Keyboard shortcuts sits in the Settings sidebar; F1 or Ctrl+, opens it. It lists every key in this map, grouped the same way, as plain dim text in Windows spelling, with labels taken from the active keyboard layout (navigator.keyboard.getLayoutMap) and localized modifier names. The panel's 'Find a setting' field searches the page by action or by key. Page-first keys carry a dim note, 'Sites can use this first'. A short 'Different from Chrome' section lists the deviations: Shift+click peeks; Shift+Enter in the address field peeks; Ctrl+Tab uses most-recent order; F6 always leaves the page; Ctrl+Q peeks. The page also has a switch, 'Shift+click a link: Peek / Open in new window', and a 'Caret browsing' switch, which has no key. Only Vitre's own verbs can be rebound, one key each: Peek (Ctrl+Q), Open as tab (Alt+Enter), Search tabs (Ctrl+Shift+A) and Download this video (Ctrl+Shift+D). Chrome-standard tab and window keys, find, navigation and editing keys are fixed. To rebind, click the key text and press the new keys; Esc cancels the capture. Each changed row gets a dim 'Reset', and the page has 'Reset all shortcuts'. The editor refuses some keys with a one-line reason: reserved keys ('Windows uses Ctrl+Shift+1 to switch input language', 'Ctrl+Alt types characters on many keyboards', 'Win keys belong to Windows', 'Microsoft Pinyin uses Ctrl+Shift+B', 'Ctrl+Esc opens Start'); single letters, bare modifiers and layout-dependent punctuation; and keys another Vitre command already uses ('Already used by Show downloads'). It warns but allows GPU-overlay defaults ('Radeon Software may use this on some PCs') and keys popular sites use ('Slack, GitHub and Notion use Ctrl+K; sites get it first'). Not in v1: a per-site 'Let this site use Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T and Ctrl+N' list for web IDEs and terminals. If it ships, it is off by default, set per site, and never covers Ctrl+Tab, F6 or Esc Esc. The refusals also cover Shift+printable keys (‘Types a character’) and Alt+letter (‘Pages use Alt+letter for access keys’), count every scope-local use as already used, and rebinding Peek or Open as tab changes every place it applies (page, peek, address field, find field). ‘Different from Chrome’ also lists Ctrl+H (recent history in the address field), F1 (keyboard shortcuts), Ctrl+Shift+D (download this video), Ctrl+Shift+T (also reopens a warm peek) and Ctrl+J (a panel, not a page). Keys some Radeon installs take (Ctrl+Shift+R, Ctrl+Shift+I) carry a dim warning.
